newsitem.title: HUNGARY: ING BARINGS MAINTAINS PICK "LT BUY" RATING.
newsitem.headline: ING BARINGS MAINTAINS PICK "LT BUY" RATING.

text.p: In a company update ING Barings said it maintained its "long-term buy" recommendation for the shares of Hungarian meat processor Pick, saying that a rebound of domestic consumption is unlikely before next year.

"Pick's interim (H1) results confirm our view that a recovery in domestic consumption is more likely in 1997, as a result of the government's recent efforts to protect Hungarians from any further decline in real wages ahead of the elections in May 1998," Gabor Sitanyi, analyst for ING Barings, said.

"Although on a prospective PER (price/earnings ratio) of 8.3 times the company is trading at a significant (17 percent) discount to the market, we are maintaining our long-term buy recommendation," he said.
This opinion was due to Pick's flat real EPS (earnings/share) growth this year and approximately seven percent real growth next year, Sitanyi said.
The beef crisis is unlikely to have any impacts on Pick's 1997 performance on its export markets, the analyst said.

The company should improve its utilisation rate of the 7,000 tonnes European Union quota for Hungarian processed meat, he said in the September publication of ING Barings' "Eastern European Equity Insights."
Pick has made what Sitanyi called "significant" efforts to penetrate the Eastern European market, but he did not expect Pick's sales to surpass 800 tonnes in the region in 1996.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange Pick shares stood at 7,020 forints at 1035 GMT.
